the development of tools and services for the automatic comparison of biological models.
the development of new algorithms for the analysis and comparison of systems biology models and with the implementation of these algorithms as software tools for modelers and biologists.
the propagation of semantic annotations in biochemical network models and with the automatic alignment of models based on these annotations.

the authors provide a new approach to model comparison and annotation assignment that can be applied to a broad range of systems biology models.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
semantic propagation is a novel approach for the propagation of biological information from annotations of individual network elements to annotations of whole models and their elements.
we provide a new method for model comparison and model annotation prediction that can help to reduce the effort required to build large-scale model collections and model databases.
semantic propagation can be used to propagate semantic information through a network, and that this is a very useful feature for model comparison and model alignment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
semantic information in biochemical reaction network models is propagated from element to element in a network, and that this can be used to improve the automatic annotation of model elements.
semantic propagation can be used to propagate information between model elements and thereby improve model annotation.
semantic propagation allows the comparison of models with different levels of annotation and the prediction of annotations for non- or partially annotated elements.
